title: आठहजार क्षेत्रका लोकगीतमा अर्थालङकार {Figure of Speech in the Folk Songs of Athahajar Region}
authors: पुन Pun, डम्बर बहादुर Dambar Bahadur
nepali: सल्यान आठहजार क्षेत्रका बाह्रमासे, पर्व, संस्कार, देवस्तुति र मौसमी गरी पाँच प्रकारका लोकगीतहरू प्रचलित छन ।यी लोकगीतमा अर्थालङ्कारको खोजी गर्नु नै यस शोध लेखको मूल उद्देश्य हो । यी लोकगीतमा अर्थालङ्कारको खोजीकालागि सर्वप्रथम लोकगीतको सङकलन गर्ने कार्य गरिएको छ । यसका लागि सम्बन्धित क्षेत्रमा गई लोकगीतको सङकलनगरिएको छ । सङकलन गरिएका लोकगीतहरूबाट उद्देश्यमूलक नमूना छनौट विधिको उपयोग गरी १५ ओटालोकगीतमा अलङ्कार खोज्ने काम यसमा गरिएको छ । अर्थालङकार पहिचान गरिएका लोकगीतको विश्लेषणको लागिनिगमनात्मक विधिको उपयोग गरिएको छ । यस शोध लेखमा उपमा, रूपक, दृष्टान्त, उत्प्रेक्षा, अतिशयोक्ति,स्वभावोक्ति, स्मृति, विभावना, विशेषोक्ति, असङगति, प्रौढोक्ति, अर्थापत्ति, विकल्प, समाधि र भाविकच्छवि अलङकारकोअध्ययन गरिएको छ । यी अलङकारका सम्बन्धमा पूर्वीय आचार्यहरूले दिएका परिभाषाहरूलाई समेत संलग्न राखेरविश्लेषण गरिएको छ । अर्थालङकारले सुशोभित यी लोकगीतहरूमा काव्यात्मकता, खोज्ने काम समेत यसमा गरिएकोछ । मूलतः यी लोकगीतमा रहेका मूल विषयहरू समाज, धर्म, संस्कृति, प्रकृति, नारी, प्रेम, विरह, जनविश्वासजस्ताविषयवस्तुको समावेश भएको पाइन्छ । यस लेखमा भने समाज र प्रेम विषयका गीतको मात्र खोजी गरिएको छ । यसक्षेत्रका लोकगीतमा खास गरेर श्रृङगार, करुण, वीर, भयानक, शान्त रसको प्रयोग भएको भए तापनि यसमा शान्त रसर करुण रसका गीतको मात्र चर्चा गरिएको छ । यी लोकगीतमा मुख्य रूपमा खसानी उपभाषिका र केही मात्रामा पर्वतीउपभाषिकाका शब्दको प्रयोग भएको पाइन्छ । संरचनाका हिसावले लोकगीतहरू ११ देखि २५ अक्षरसम्मका पाइन्छन ।
american_english: Five types of folk songs are prevalent in the Salyan Athahajar region: perennial (bahramase), festival, ceremonial, devotional hymns to deities, and seasonal. The primary objective of this research paper is to investigate figures of sense (arthalankara) in these folk songs. To search for figures of sense in these folk songs, the work of collecting folk songs was carried out first. For this purpose, folk songs were collected by visiting the relevant region. From the collected folk songs, using a purposive sampling method, figures of speech were investigated in 15 folk songs. A deductive method has been utilized for analyzing the folk songs in which figures of sense were identified. In this research paper, the figures of speech Upama (simile), Rupaka (metaphor), Drishtanta (exemplification), Utpreksha (poetic fancy), Atishayokti (hyperbole), Svabhavokti (natural description), Smriti (recollection), Vibhavana (peculiar causation), Visheshokti (peculiar non-effect), Asangati (incongruity), Praudhokti (bold assertion), Arthapatti (presumption), Vikalpa (alternative), Samadhi (concurrent cause), and Bhavikachhavi have been studied. The analysis has been performed by also incorporating the definitions provided by Eastern classical masters concerning these figures of speech. An exploration of poetic quality in these folk songs embellished with figures of sense has also been undertaken here. Essentially, the core subject matter in these folk songs is found to include themes such as society, religion, culture, nature, women, love, separation, and popular beliefs. In this paper, however, an investigation has been conducted only into songs dealing with the themes of society and love. Although Shringara, Karuna, Vira, Bhayanaka, and Shanta rasas are particularly employed in the folk songs of this region, only songs of Shanta rasa and Karuna rasa are discussed here. In these folk songs, words from the Khasani sub-dialect are predominantly found to be used, along with a small proportion of words from the Parbati sub-dialect. Structurally, the folk songs are found to contain between 11 and 25 syllables.

informal_english: In the Salyan Athahajar region, five types of folk songs are on the go: year-round tunes (bahramase), festival ones, rituals, devotional hymns to deities, and seasonal songs. Tracking down figures of sense (arthalankara) in these folk songs is the main point of this research paper. To look for figures of sense in these folk songs, collecting folk songs was done first up. For this, folk songs were gathered by heading right out to the relevant area. From the collected folk songs, figures of speech were tracked down in 15 folk songs using purposive sampling. A deductive method has been used to analyse the folk songs where figures of sense were identified. In this research paper, the figures of speech Upama (simile), Rupaka (metaphor), Drishtanta (illustration), Utpreksha (poetic fancy), Atishayokti (hyperbole), Svabhavokti (natural description), Smriti (recollection), Vibhavana (peculiar causation), Visheshokti (peculiar non-effect), Asangati (incongruity), Praudhokti (bold assertion), Arthapatti (presumption), Vikalpa (alternative), Samadhi (concurrent cause), and Bhavikachhavi have been studied. The analysis was done while also bringing in definitions given by Eastern classical masters on these figures of speech. Checking for poetic quality in these folk songs decked out with figures of sense was also tackled here. Basically, the core themes in these folk songs cover stuff like society, religion, culture, nature, women, love, heartbreak, and folk beliefs. But in this paper, only songs on society and love were looked into. Even though Shringara, Karuna, Vira, Bhayanaka, and Shanta rasas are especially used in the folk songs of this area, only songs of Shanta rasa and Karuna rasa are discussed here. In these folk songs, words from the Khasani sub-dialect are mainly found to be used, alongside a handful of words from the Parbati sub-dialect. Structure-wise, the folk songs are found to run from 11 to 25 syllables.
